page: Amazon Web Services g6f.large is an entry-level accelerated computing instance provisioned on the Nitro hypervisor. The compute slice is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz with x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 threads. Memory allocation consists of 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, backed by 4 MB of L3 cache. For local high-speed operations, the instance includes a 100 GB NVMe SSD, while network communication runs on a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via a fractional NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, providing 0.125 of a GPU and 3 GB of dedicated VRAM. In benchmark testing, this fractional accelerator demonstrates moderate capacity for smaller machine learning inference tasks, reaching 1089.99 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 69.08 tokens per second on a 7B model. However, generation speeds on the 135M model register at a lower 43.54 tokens per second, and large 70B models are unsupported due to the restricted VRAM footprint.

CPU and memory throughput reveal the limitations of the instance's 1-core allocation. While stress-ng single-core performance ranks in the top 25% at 2870.48, multi-core output remains identical, placing it in the bottom 25%. Synthetic suites reflect low aggregate throughput: Geekbench multi-core registers at 1179.0, PassMark CPU reaches 3459.75, and memory bandwidth drops to 20.45 GB/s on large read blocks. Application-level metrics indicate constrained capacity, yielding 2.38 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 2.85 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

By offering fractional access to an enterprise Ada Lovelace GPU alongside local NVMe storage, the g6f.large provides a low-entry hardware cost footprint for GPU-accelerated computing. It is structurally targeted at lightweight GPU tasks that do not justify a full accelerator, such as entry-level graphics rendering, small-model inference, video transcoding, and development testing.
description: Amazon Web Services g6f.large is an accelerated computing instance featuring 2 vCPUs from a single physical core on a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. It integrates 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a dedicated 100 GB NVMe SSD, and 2 Gbps baseline networking on the Nitro hypervisor. Acceleration is supplied by a fractional 0.125 NVIDIA L4 GPU with 3 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results exhibit solid single-core performance (stress-ng score of 2870.48) but limited multi-core throughput due to the dual-thread core configuration. In machine learning testing, the instance achieves 1089.99 tokens per second for prompt processing on 135M parameter models and 69.08 tokens per second on 7B models. Given the modest compute density and constrained GPU footprint, the g6f.large functions efficiently for lightweight inference, graphics workloads, and development prototyping without the expense of an entire GPU accelerator.
